|---------|-----------|------------|

**Analysis:** The most distinctive feature of the test image is the **overall silvery/bronze leaf discoloration** combined with **scattered dark spots** and **dark necrotic area near the growing tip**. This triad is most characteristic of Tomato Spotted Wilt Virus (TSWV), which causes bronze/silver leaf discoloration (from thrips feeding), dark circular lesions, and necrotic streaks on stems and petioles.

The TSWV reference images (Bugwood_136, 144) didn't show the classic leaf bronzing well, but the symptom combination in the test image — pale/silvery leaves, dark spots, and growing-tip necrosis — aligns most strongly with TSWV. Bacterial Speck was somewhat similar in spotting pattern but lacked the overall bronzing. Septoria showed spots on still-green leaves. None of the other candidates explained the full symptom profile.
